items.q: In the mid oesophageal four chamber view, which multiplane angle shows the target best?
items.exp: The mid oesophageal four chamber view opens at close to 0 degrees, where four chambers with the septa horizontal on screen. Other angles cut the plane obliquely. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on standard views and multiplane angles.

items.q: Which structure must be clearly seen in the mid oesophageal four chamber view?
o: Aortic arch with head and neck branches
Left ventricular apex in long axis
Right pulmonary veins in long axis
Four chambers with the septa horizontal on screen
items.exp: The mid oesophageal four chamber view is defined by four chambers with the septa horizontal on screen, which serves global function and chamber size at the mid level. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: In the mid oesophageal two chamber view, which multiplane angle shows the target best?
items.exp: The mid oesophageal two chamber view opens at close to 90 degrees, where anterior and inferior walls with the left atrial appendage. Other angles cut the plane obliquely. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on standard views and multiplane angles.

items.q: Which structure must be clearly seen in the mid oesophageal two chamber view?
o: Hepatic vein joining the inferior vena cava
Aortic arch with head and neck branches
Right pulmonary veins in long axis
Anterior and inferior walls with the left atrial appendage
items.exp: The mid oesophageal two chamber view is defined by anterior and inferior walls with the left atrial appendage, which serves left atrial appendage check for thrombus. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: In the mid oesophageal long axis view, which multiplane angle shows the target best?
items.exp: The mid oesophageal long axis view opens at close to 120 degrees, where aortic valve with the outflow tract in long axis. Other angles cut the plane obliquely. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on standard views and multiplane angles.

items.q: Which structure must be clearly seen in the mid oesophageal long axis view?
o: Aortic arch with head and neck branches
Left ventricular apex in long axis
Right pulmonary veins in long axis
Aortic valve with the outflow tract in long axis
items.exp: The mid oesophageal long axis view is defined by aortic valve with the outflow tract in long axis, which serves aortic valve disease and outflow assessment. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: In the mid oesophageal bicaval view, which multiplane angle shows the target best?
items.exp: The mid oesophageal bicaval view opens at close to 90 degrees, where superior and inferior vena cava entering the right atrium. Other angles cut the plane obliquely. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on standard views and multiplane angles.

items.q: Which structure must be clearly seen in the mid oesophageal bicaval view?
o: Hepatic vein joining the inferior vena cava
Aortic arch with head and neck branches
Right pulmonary veins in long axis
Superior and inferior vena cava entering the right atrium
items.exp: The mid oesophageal bicaval view is defined by superior and inferior vena cava entering the right atrium, which serves atrial septum check for shunts and lines. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: In the mid oesophageal aortic short axis view, which multiplane angle shows the target best?
items.exp: The mid oesophageal aortic short axis view opens at close to 45 degrees, where aortic valve in cross section with three cusps. Other angles cut the plane obliquely. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on standard views and multiplane angles.

items.q: Which structure must be clearly seen in the mid oesophageal aortic short axis view?
o: Aortic arch with head and neck branches
Left ventricular apex in long axis
Right pulmonary veins in long axis
Aortic valve in cross section with three cusps
items.exp: The mid oesophageal aortic short axis view is defined by aortic valve in cross section with three cusps, which serves cusp number and opening before surgery. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: In the mid oesophageal aortic long axis view, which multiplane angle shows the target best?
items.exp: The mid oesophageal aortic long axis view opens at close to 120 degrees, where aortic root with the valve in long axis. Other angles cut the plane obliquely. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on standard views and multiplane angles.

items.q: Which structure must be clearly seen in the mid oesophageal aortic long axis view?
o: Hepatic vein joining the inferior vena cava
Aortic arch with head and neck branches
Right pulmonary veins in long axis
Aortic root with the valve in long axis
items.exp: The mid oesophageal aortic long axis view is defined by aortic root with the valve in long axis, which serves root size and regurgitant jet direction. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: In the transgastric mid short axis view, which multiplane angle shows the target best?
items.exp: The transgastric mid short axis view opens at close to 0 degrees, where left ventricle in cross section at papillary level. Other angles cut the plane obliquely. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on standard views and multiplane angles.

items.q: Which structure must be clearly seen in the transgastric mid short axis view?
o: Aortic arch with head and neck branches
Left ventricular apex in long axis
Right pulmonary veins in long axis
Left ventricle in cross section at papillary level
items.exp: The transgastric mid short axis view is defined by left ventricle in cross section at papillary level, which serves wall motion and volume monitoring during surgery. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: In the descending aorta short axis view, which multiplane angle shows the target best?
o: Close to 0 degrees with probe rotation
items.exp: The descending aorta short axis view opens at close to 0 degrees with probe rotation, where descending aorta in cross section behind the heart. Other angles cut the plane obliquely. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on standard views and multiplane angles.

items.q: Which structure must be clearly seen in the descending aorta short axis view?
o: Hepatic vein joining the inferior vena cava
Aortic arch with head and neck branches
Right pulmonary veins in long axis
Descending aorta in cross section behind the heart
items.exp: The descending aorta short axis view is defined by descending aorta in cross section behind the heart, which serves dissection flap and plaque check along the vessel. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on required landmarks for each view.

items.q: Before a planned transoesophageal study, what preparation best reduces aspiration risk?
o: Remove monitoring to keep the patient calm
Keep the patient nil by mouth as the local protocol states
Give a full meal one hour before
items.exp: An empty stomach keeps regurgitated contents low, so fasting per protocol is the key safety step before probe insertion. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on patient preparation and safety.

items.q: Which history is a reason to defer transoesophageal echo and seek another test?
o: Known oesophageal stricture or varices with bleeding risk
items.exp: Stricture, varices, tumour or prior perforation raise injury risk, so the probe must not pass until the risk is cleared. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on contraindications.

items.q: What is the purpose of the bite guard during transoesophageal echo?
o: Protect the teeth and the probe shaft from biting damage
items.exp: Biting can injure teeth and ruin the probe, so the guard stays in place whenever the probe is in the mouth. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on probe handling.

items.q: During probe insertion the patient gags. What is the safest response?
o: Ask the patient to swallow forcefully without pause
Pause, use jaw thrust and gentle anteflexion with steady guidance
items.exp: Force risks perforation, so pause and reposition with jaw support and gentle flexion until the probe passes smoothly. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on probe insertion technique.

items.q: Why is the left atrial appendage studied carefully during TEE in atrial fibrillation?
o: Thrombus there can embolise at cardioversion
items.exp: Slow flow in fibrillation lets clot form in the appendage, so confirming it is clear guides safe cardioversion. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on left atrial appendage imaging.

items.q: Which TEE view best shows the atrial septum for a shunt check?
o: Mid oesophageal aortic short axis view
items.exp: The bicaval plane cuts both cavae with the septum between them, so colour across it reveals the shunt directly. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on atrial septum imaging.

items.q: TEE is requested for suspected endocarditis with poor transthoracic windows. Why is TEE the better test?
o: It needs no sedation or monitoring
The probe lies close behind the heart with higher frequency detail
items.exp: Closeness to the posterior heart with a higher frequency probe resolves small vegetations that surface echo misses. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on indications.

items.q: What monitoring is expected during sedated transoesophageal echo?
o: Pulse oximetry with blood pressure and ECG rhythm checks
No monitoring once the probe is in
items.exp: Sedation can depress breathing and pressure, so oxygen saturation, pressure and rhythm are watched throughout. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on sedation and monitoring with anaesthesia support.

items.q: Which finding on TEE best supports an aortic dissection flap?
o: A thick aortic wall with no moving part
A mobile linear echo inside the aortic lumen with flow on both sides
A fixed bright ring at the valve
A small echo free space behind the heart
items.exp: A flap moves independently within the lumen with true and false channels, unlike fixed wall thickening or simple fluid. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on aortic imaging.

items.q: Why does the TEE probe use a higher frequency than the surface probe?
o: The oesophagus lies close to the heart so penetration matters less
Frequency has no effect on image quality
items.exp: Short distance to the target lets higher frequency give finer detail, while surface echo needs lower frequency to reach deep. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on instrumentation.

items.q: After TEE the patient has chest pain with surgical emphysema. What must be excluded first?
items.exp: Perforation is rare but dangerous, so new pain with air under the skin after instrumentation needs urgent assessment. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on complications.

items.q: Which view monitors left ventricular function continuously during cardiac surgery?
items.exp: The transgastric short axis cuts the ventricle at papillary level and stays stable, so wall motion and filling are watched beat to beat. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on perioperative monitoring.

items.q: A patient in atrial fibrillation is planned for cardioversion. What TEE finding is needed before cardioversion can proceed under guideline directed anticoagulation with the team?
o: No thrombus in the left atrium or appendage with good emptying
items.exp: Clear atrium and appendage with active emptying means no clot to dislodge, but TEE clearance alone is not enough and cardioversion proceeds only with guideline directed periprocedural anticoagulation decided with the team. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on cardioversion assessment, with anticoagulation per the ESC atrial fibrillation guideline.

items.q: Why is consent for TEE more detailed than for surface echo?
o: It is semi invasive with sedation, perforation and dental risks
items.exp: Passing a probe into the oesophagus with sedation carries small but real risks, so benefits and harms must be explained and recorded. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on consent.

items.q: Which probe motion turns the image plane from short axis toward long axis at one probe tip position?
items.exp: The multiplane control steers the crystal angle from 0 toward 180 degrees, so the plane rotates without moving the tip. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on probe manipulation.

items.q: The descending aorta view shows bright plaque with shadowing. Why does it matter?
o: Mobile or bulky plaque raises embolic risk during catheter and surgical work
items.exp: Bulky atheroma can embolise when wires or clamps pass, so its site and mobility are reported before procedures. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on aortic atheroma.
